Timeline::where¶

Back to Timeline API Reference

Signature¶

Timeline::where(const Series& mask, const Timeline& other) -> Timeline

What It Does¶

Builds a new timeline by choosing between self and other under a boolean mask.

Current verified behavior is:

  • where mask is true, keep self

  • where mask is false, take other

That matters because this is easy to assume backwards if you are coming from a different mental model. The verified output below is the authoritative behavior for the current implementation.

Parameters¶

mask

A boolean Series that is broadcast against the timeline operands.

Use it when you already computed a predicate such as isnat(), lt(...), or is_weekend().

other

The alternate timeline to draw from where the mask is false.

This may be a scalar or a shaped timeline as long as broadcast rules can align it with self.

Returns¶

Timeline A new timeline assembled from the two temporal operands.

Examples¶

Example 1. Keep the original values where they are missing and otherwise take a date-normalized replacement.

auto out = with_nat.where(with_nat.isnat(), with_nat.floor("D"));
std::cout << pluss::timeline::print(out) << "\n";

Output¶

Timeline(shape=[4], tz=UTC)
[ 2024-11-01 00:00:00, NaT, 2024-12-31 00:00:00, NaT ]

This verified output shows the mask is selecting self where the predicate is true.

Notes¶

  • where() is the general branch/choose surface.

  • For the narrower task “replace only missing timestamps with one scalar timestamp”, fill_nat is more direct.

  • The mask must be boolean. Passing a numeric Series is a contract error.
